newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-IN-FORM FULKE SECURES OPEN BERTH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-IN-FORM FULKE SECURES OPEN BERTH.

text.p: Sweden's Pierre Fulke, who produced the most impressive performance of his career in finishing joint fourth in last week's Loch Lomond World Invitational, has another chance to take on the game's elite after qualifying on Monday for the British Open.

Fulke shot two successive 69s on the Western Gailes course and initially thought it might only put him into a playoff but it proved just enough. "I played okay and there were not too many mistakes," he said.

Warren Bladon, former British amateur champion, pitched in from 59 yards for an eagle to snatch the final qualifying place from the Western Gailes course when he was involved in a playoff with former Ryder Cup player Barry Lane.
Both had finished on 139 and were still level after two playoff holes but on the third, a par five, Bladon's chip brought a dramatic finish.
Australian veteran Rodger Davis, celebrating his 20th year on the European Tour, also gained a place in the Open starting line-up on Thursday.
He had rounds of 69 and 67 on the Irvine course and said: "I'm a nervous wreck. It's easier playing in the Open itself."
American Larry Mize, 1987 U.S. Masters champion, was less fortunate, his two-round 142 at Western Gailes leaving him down the field.
"I missed a couple of putts at the first two holes which could have been a nice way to start, but it wasn't to be and that was pretty much the story of the round," he said.
"Obviously I'm disappointed at not making the British Open. I've had to qualify before so it's not a new experience for me, but it doesn't make it any easier."
